attempts.reason: The CORS setting is now right: the browser's preflight passed. The upload itself (PUT to the presigned link) still failed. The browser reports that the PUT's answer carries no Access-Control-Allow-Origin, and no longer says the preflight failed (the 05:29 attempt did). The page showed "Your file couldn't be uploaded".
attempts.probableCause: Not confirmed. The presigned link carries x-amz-checksum-crc32=AAAAAA== (the CRC32 of an EMPTY body) and x-amz-sdk-checksum-algorithm=CRC32; the 05:29 link carried the same. The AWS SDK in use (client-s3 and s3-request-presigner 3.1125.0) adds these by default and src/server/services/storage-service.ts does not turn that off. The uploaded file is not empty, so the storage service most likely rejects the PUT for a checksum mismatch, and its error answers carry no CORS headers (a PUT with no signature answers 400 with no Access-Control-Allow-Origin for the preview, the production and the localhost origins alike), which the browser shows as a CORS block. Local MinIO accepts the same kind of link (the local full journey passed).
attempts.notConfirmedBecause: The storage service's real answer to the PUT could not be read: the browser hides it, and replaying the request outside the browser was not permitted in this session.
attempts.scope: A product fault in the upload link, not a test fault and not the CORS setting. It would affect uploads from the production address too. Not fixed here: a fix changes src/server/services/storage-service.ts and reaches the preview only through a push and a rebuild.

attempts.reason: The checksum fix is deployed and works as designed: the link has no checksum parameter. The storage service still refuses the browser's PUT, and the answer still carries no Access-Control-Allow-Origin, so the browser hides the status and the body. The empty-body checksum was therefore not the cause, or not the only cause.
attempts.causeNotEstablished: The storage service's real answer to the PUT was not read in this attempt either (the browser hides it; the request was not replayed outside the browser). What is known: CORS preflight passes for the exact object address; the link is a plain SigV4 presigned PutObject with only the host header signed; storage error answers carry no CORS headers whatever the reason (shown in the 07:49 session with an unsigned PUT). Candidates that fit, none tested: the storage credentials on the preview being refused (wrong secret, or a token without write permission on this bucket), or a bucket or endpoint value on the preview that does not match. To tell them apart someone must read the status and error code of the PUT: the Network tab of the browser on the preview shows the status code, or one server-side storage call with the preview's credentials.

attempts.whatThisProves: On the deploy preview a browser upload to hosted storage succeeds, the server reads the stored file back, a certificate PDF is in storage and is downloaded through a link the preview presigned, and the public verification page reports it valid. So the storage key and secret now reach the preview's functions, belong together, and may read and write the bucket. Which request wrote the PDF was not traced; the task runner on this machine had no S3 variables in its environment (names checked, not values), so the write is taken to have been made by the preview's own functions (inference).
attempts.whatThisDoesNotProve: Nothing about the Production context in Netlify (its storage keys are not verified). It is one run by a test, not the unassisted manual journey by a person (D-08).
